page: Microsoft Azure E20s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 20 dedicated vCPUs backed by 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The host CPU incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized vector and cryptographic instructions, including AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 160.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local ephemeral storage is not included, requiring remote network storage for all disk persistence, and no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark measurements place the processor and memory subsystem in the middle quartile of overall performance tiers. The compute tier achieves a multi-core stress-ng score of 19310.24, a multi-core Geekbench score of 11021.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 25434.63. Memory throughput measures 113.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 60.71 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Practical workload testing shows 19.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 24.79 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. CPU-driven inference runs at 1382.78 prompt tokens per second on lightweight 135M parameter models, declining to 4.22 prompt tokens per second on large 70B models.

Cost efficiency is directed toward capacity-heavy workloads where RAM density outweighs the demand for raw compute scaling or local scratch drive IOPS. Relying completely on external storage introduces network storage latency tradeoffs that must be planned for in I/O design. The hardware composition fits memory-intensive enterprise tasks, such as in-memory databases, Redis caches, business application processing, and relational database hosting.
description: The Microsoft Azure E20s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 20 dedicated vCPUs and 10 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Designed around an x86_64 architecture, the instance pairs 160.0 GB of system memory with 260 MB of L3 cache, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It contains no local ephemeral storage, depending entirely on remote storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware or bundled public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks reveal mid-range performance, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 11021.0, 113.56 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, and 19.46 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based text generation is capable for compact language models but drops significantly on large 70B models. The server provides balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy requirements, making it suitable for in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, medium-scale analytics processing, and business application backends.
